comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the claims about Bonus requirement in early oogenesis (C2, C19-C27, C75, C115-C122). OpenEval emphasizes experimental rigor (sample sizes, controls, multiple approaches), while peer reviewers affirm the findings are 'convincing' and identify this as a 'previously unknown function.' Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluations support the RNA-seq identification of Bonus target genes (C28-C33, C76-C77, C123-C131). OpenEval highlights statistical rigor and validation methods, while peer reviewers explicitly list target gene identification as a strength. Both accept the tissue-specificity and lack of TE upregulation. Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Perfect agreement on H3K9me3 deposition mechanism (C4, C35-C38, C132-C135, C163). Both evaluations accept the tethering and ChIP data showing H3K9me3 accumulation. OpenEval notes appropriate interpretation of genes lacking H3K9me3 changes, peer reviewers affirm this as showing the repression mechanism. Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Strong agreement on Bonus interactions with Mi-2/NuRD and SetDB1 (C5-C8, C39-C45, C83, C139-C140). Both evaluations accept the co-IP and functional data. OpenEval emphasizes negative controls and domain mapping, peer reviewers list this as a key strength showing physical interactions mediating repression. Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluations support identification of K20 as the conserved SUMOylation site (C9-C11, C46-C52, C144-C146). OpenEval details the multiple lines of evidence (mutagenesis, phylogenetics, biochemistry), peer reviewers explicitly list K20 identification and conservation as a strength. Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluations support the SUMOylation-dependent localization findings (C12-C14, C54-C61, C151, C157, C173-C174). OpenEval emphasizes fractionation and co-IP data, peer reviewers note the 'interesting' mislocalization of K20-mutant in nuclear puncta. Both accept the localization data as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations address functional requirement of SUMOylation for repression (C62-C67). OpenEval groups this with localization data in R6, while peer reviewers separate it as R7. Both accept the reporter assay and SetDB1 interaction data showing SUMOylation is required for repression. Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluations support Su(var)2-10 as the E3 ligase for Bonus (C15, C68-C74, C162). OpenEval details the co-IP and stabilization data, peer reviewers explicitly list this as a strength. Both accept the knockdown and functional validation data. Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluations support the evolutionary interpretation and comparative analysis with mammalian KAP-1 (C16-C18, C53, C84-C87, C175). OpenEval notes the claim is inferential and could benefit from more phylogenetic analysis, while peer reviewers accept this as showing 'prototypical modes of regulation.' Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluations address the indirect regulation mechanism (C78-C79, C164). OpenEval rates this as SUPPORTED but notes mechanisms remain speculative, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting the study would be strengthened by demonstrating direct recruitment. This represents a difference in evaluation stringency on the same claims.

Both evaluations support the finding that ple is expressed in follicular cells (C34, C80). OpenEval groups this with indirect regulation claims, peer reviewers treat it separately. Both accept the in situ HCR data without challenge. Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluations support the finding that Bonus depletion does not upregulate TEs (C81-C82). OpenEval includes this in the broader RNA-seq result (R2), peer reviewers treat it separately (R13). Both accept this as distinguishing Bonus from piRNA pathway components. Both agree on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluations identify speculative claims about K20R mutant function (C88). OpenEval rates multiple speculative claims as UNCERTAIN (C114, C152, C154-C155, C159, C169-C170), while peer reviewers focus specifically on C88, noting the 3KR data partially addresses concerns but single K20R testing would strengthen conclusions. Both agree on UNCERTAIN status for overlapping claims.

OpenEval rates claims about cytoplasmic export and nuclear foci interpretations (C152, C154-C155) as UNCERTAIN/speculative, while peer reviewers rate the broader localization findings (which include these claims) as SUPPORTED in R6. This represents different granularity in evaluation—peer reviewers accept the overall localization data while OpenEval flags specific mechanistic interpretations as speculative.

OpenEval R10 includes background/citation claims (C136-C138, C141-C142) about NuRD and SetDB1 as SUPPORTED knowledge claims, while peer reviewers incorporate these same claims into their evaluation of the experimental interaction data (R4). Both accept these as valid contextual information.

OpenEval R10 includes background citations about mammalian KAP-1 SUMOylation (C160-C161) as SUPPORTED knowledge claims, while peer reviewers incorporate these into their evaluation of the evolutionary comparison (R8). Both accept these as appropriate literature context.

OpenEval R10 extensively catalogs background knowledge and citation claims (C1, C89-C113, C136-C143, C147-C148, C150, C153, C156, C158, C165-C168, C171) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these contextual/citation claims, instead incorporating relevant background into their assessments of experimental findings.

OpenEval flags C159 (stabilized E3 complex) as UNCERTAIN/speculative without direct demonstration. Peer reviewers include this claim in their SUPPORTED evaluation of Su(var)2-10 as E3 ligase (R8), accepting the mechanistic interpretation based on the K20R mutant data showing trapped intermediate.
